newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: World Court says it will hear Iran vs U.S. case.
newsitem.headline: World Court says it will hear Iran vs U.S. case.

text.p: The International Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that it could hear a dispute over attacks on Iranian oil platforms by U.S. warships in the 1980s.
The decision is an initial victory for Tehran and a setback for Washington in a long and complex legal battle between the arch-foes over events which occurred almost 10 years ago.
Iran wants the U.N. court to rule that the destruction of its oil platforms in October 1987 and April 1988 violated international law and that the United States should pay damages.
Washington had urged the judges to throw the case out, arguing that the strikes were a legitimate response to attacks on a U.S. frigate and an oil tanker sailing under the U.S. flag.
The disputed events date back to the final stages of the 1980-88 war between Iran and Iraq when the U.S. sent naval forces to the Gulf to protect international shipping.

The Hague-based court ruled on Thursday that a 1955 Treaty of Amity between Iran and the United States provided a basis for its jurisdiction over the case and will hold further proceedings to consider the issues at the heart of the dispute.
